category_title: Mature students with depression and insomnia focused on vocational progression
minimal_context: Colin is participating in a specialized cookery course where he needs to chop onions and add them to a recipe at the right time.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Colin, please chop the onions and put them in at the right time for the recipe.

STUDENT: I'm not sure when they go in... I have a fear of failure and I'm worried the other students will laugh at me if I make a mistake.

TUTOR: Colin, just follow the instructions on the page.

STUDENT: (Colin looks down at the onions, feeling embarrassment about asking for help. He stares blankly, exhausted from severe insomnia and depression.)

TUTOR: Colin, I am talking to you. Why are you just standing there?

STUDENT: You really showed me up! I didn't realise you were talking to me. That done it for me. I'm leaving and I'm never going back.

options.A: Allow Colin to make mistakes with the recipe without making a big issue out of it.
options.B: Terminate the task demands and remove the onions and recipe materials for 10 seconds.
options.C: Ask probing questions about the ingredients, such as 'What are you checking to see?' and 'How many onions fit?'
options.D: Ask iterative 'why' and 'how' questions (e.g., 'Why do you feel you need to leave?', 'How does making a mistake feel?').
